# math/rand

> Random numbers: a seedable generator (xorshift64*) for games, shuffles and tests. Not for secrets.

truck [math](../math.md) · [source](../../../registry/math/rand.pkg)

```
rand_seed(42)                  // the same numbers every run
print rand_int(6) + 1          // a die roll
print rand_range(10, 20)       // 10 to 20, both included
let xs = make([int], 5)
for i = 0 to 4
  xs[i] = i
end
rand_shuffle(xs)
rand_seed_time()               // different numbers every run
```

| function | gives |
|---|---|
| `rand_seed(s: int)` | start the sequence from `s`; the same seed gives the same numbers on every backend |
| `rand_seed_time()` | seed from the clock |
| `rand_bits() -> int` | 64 random bits (any `int`, negative too) |
| `rand_int(n: int) -> int` | `0` to `n - 1`, every value equally likely; 0 if `n <= 0` |
| `rand_range(lo: int, hi: int) -> int` | `lo` to `hi`, both included |
| `rand_bool() -> bool` | true or false |
| `rand_chance(num: int, den: int) -> bool` | true with probability `num / den` |
| `rand_shuffle(xs: [int])` | put `xs` in a random order (Fisher–Yates) |

Without a seed, the sequence is the one for seed 0. The generator is
fast and good enough for simulations, but predictable: don't use it for
passwords or keys (read `/dev/urandom` for those).

## Library code

Merged into every program that uses this package.

```
global rand_state: int = 0
global rand_seeded: bool = false

// splitmix64: spreads any seed over the 64 bits
fn rand_mix(x: int) -> int
  let z = x
  z = (z ^ math_ushr(z, 30)) * -4658895280553007687
  z = (z ^ math_ushr(z, 27)) * -7723592293110705685
  return z ^ math_ushr(z, 31)
end

fn rand_seed(s: int)
  rand_state = rand_mix(s + -7046029254386353131)
  if rand_state == 0
    rand_state = 1
  end
  rand_seeded = true
end

fn rand_seed_time()
  rand_seed(time_now())
end

fn rand_bits() -> int
  if !rand_seeded
    rand_seed(0)
  end
  let x = rand_state
  x = x ^ math_ushr(x, 12)
  x = x ^ (x << 25)
  x = x ^ math_ushr(x, 27)
  rand_state = x
  return x * 2685821657736338717
end

fn rand_int(n: int) -> int
  if n <= 0
    return 0
  end
  // reject the top values that would make some results likelier
  let lim = MATH_MAX - MATH_MAX % n
  while true
    let r = math_ushr(rand_bits(), 1)
    if r < lim
      return r % n
    end
  end
  return 0
end

fn rand_range(lo: int, hi: int) -> int
  if hi <= lo
    return lo
  end
  return lo + rand_int(hi - lo + 1)
end

fn rand_bool() -> bool
  return rand_bits() < 0
end

fn rand_chance(num: int, den: int) -> bool
  return rand_int(den) < num
end

fn rand_shuffle(xs: [int])
  let i = len(xs) - 1
  while i > 0
    let j = rand_int(i + 1)
    let t = xs[i]
    xs[i] = xs[j]
    xs[j] = t
    i = i - 1
  end
end
```
